Connecticut Delaware Florida Georgia Hawaii Idaho Illinois Indiana Iowa Kansas Kentucky Louisiana Maine Maryland Massachusetts Michigan Minnesota Mississippi Missouri Montana Nebraska Nevada New Hampshire New Jersey New Mexico New York North Carolina North Dakota Ohio Oklahoma Oregon Pennsylvania Puerto Rico Rhode Island South Carolina South Dakota Tennessee Texas Utah Vermont Virginia Washington West Virginia Wisconsin Wyoming Find Schools Answer: University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC) is not classified as a Historically Black College or University (HBCU) by the United States Department of Education. Located in Baltimore, Maryland, UMBC has a student population of more than 13,000 and offers more than 100 degree programs. Although it is not classified as an HBCU, UMBC is ranked nationally as the #1 school for African American undergraduates who go on to complete an M.D./Ph.D. and UMBC is ranked #2 for African American undergraduates who complete a science or engineering Ph.D. Maryland is home to more than 80 colleges and universities. Below is a list of the four HBCUs located in the state of Maryland: Bowie State University - Bowie, Maryland Coppin State University - Baltimore, Maryland Morgan State University - Baltimore, Maryland University of Maryland Eastern Shore - Princess Anne, Maryland HBCUs are recognized by the United States Department of Education as nationally accredited colleges and universities established before 1964 whose mission is to educate African Americans.
